geo.label: recession scare / tariff shock
parts: Macro Stance

Bearish. The S&P 500 closed at 5,572.07 on the 11 March session, down 3.57% over five sessions and 8.15% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). CNBC reported that most of the index is already in correction territory [[n11556]], and WSJ framed the Nasdaq's worst day since 2022 as investors weighing a possible recession [[n11557]]. The Nasdaq 100 is down 10.94% over 20 sessions to 19,376.96, and the Russell 2000 is down 11.55% to 2,023.59 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Citi downgraded US stocks as Wall Street suffered its worst drop in years [[n11510]], and Goldman Sachs slashed its US economic forecasts as tariff impacts grew 'considerably more adverse' [[n10999]]. The VIX closed at 26.92, up 70.27% over 20 sessions from 15.81 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). This is a growth scare first, and the bond market is confirming it.
Rates & Curve

The US Treasury par curve at the 11 March close has the 2-year at 3.94% and the 10-year at 4.28% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-11), a 10Y-2Y spread of +34 bps. The curve is positively sloped. Over 20 observations the 2-year is down 34 bps and the 10-year down 23 bps, so the spread widened 11 bps in a bull steepening led by the front end (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-11). That is growth insurance being bought, not inflation being feared. The dollar index is at 103.44 index points, down 4.51% over 20 sessions from 108.32 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), so the dollar is not acting as the safe-haven bid this time. The 10Y-3M spread is minus 6 bps and the 30Y-10Y spread is plus 31 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-11).
New / Most Important

The most important signal is the collision between a funding fight and a tariff drumbeat. The House passed a spending bill to avert a shutdown and sent it to the Senate [[n11535]], and Senate Democrats now face what ABC called a 'stark' choice [[n11499]]. On tariffs, House Republicans blocked Congress from challenging Trump's tariffs [[n11537]], Trump doubled metals tariffs and then backed off [[n5046]], and the Canada hike was reversed after Ontario lifted its electricity threat [[n11587]]. The labour market is not the problem yet: job openings rose to 7.7 million in January [[n11142]]. Airlines cut their forecasts, citing softer consumer confidence [[n9001]], and that is where the data and the tape meet. A firm labour print with a shrinking consumer outlook is the mix that keeps the Fed on hold while equities reprice.
Playbook ✓

Bearish. Keep equity beta light into the Senate vote, and buy protection rather than chase the bounce. Own the front end of the Treasury curve, where the bull steepening is concentrated, and stay underweight the dollar. Avoid consumer-discretionary names and cyclical financials where guidance is being cut. The call changes if the S&P 500 closes back above its 20-session reference of 6,066.44, which would mean the correction is being repaired rather than bounced through, or if a Senate deal removes the shutdown tail without new tariff escalation.

geo.label: fiscal boost vs tariff drag
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. The European Central Bank cut its key rate to 2.5%, citing what DW quoted as 'risk, uncertainty' [[n3489]]. JPMorgan joined Goldman Sachs in raising its euro-area growth forecast for 2025 [[n3643]], which fits the German spending turn. Euro strength is the dollar story rather than a growth verdict: EUR/USD closed at 1.0839, up 5.22% over 20 sessions from 1.0302 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and the Guardian reported euro and pound gains amid 'Trumpcession' fears [[n3679]]. Equities have not followed the fiscal story. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 5,309.90, down 1.50% over 20 sessions, and the STOXX 600 fell to 536.89, down 1.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Activity & Inflation

German fiscal expansion is the growth driver in the headlines. Reuters argued the German spending boost will leave a lasting mark on world bond markets [[n3634]], while the Bundesbank warned that more German spending is justified but is 'not a cure all' [[n3651]]. Bund safe-haven status is holding in swap markets, though worries about the size of the German spending surge are growing [[n3677]]. Hedge funds fleeing positions dented European stock traders, according to sources cited by Reuters [[n3683]], which fits an equity tape weaker than the fiscal narrative. Le Monde's headline frames military spending as a stimulant for growth, and for inflation [[n3687]], so the inflation side of the trade is already on the table.
New / Most Important

EU ministers backed a proposal for a temporary exemption on defence spending in the EU's fiscal rules [[n5614]]. That is the rule change that matters most, because it lets national defence budgets grow without the deficit framework doing all the policing. Politico reported that Germany's Merz has two weeks to deliver a historic spending revolution [[n3562]], and Reuters said the 'Merz spurt' will make European CEOs rethink their US pivot [[n3582]]. In France the picture is less clean. Euronews reported that Macron's defence spending plan is driving open political divisions [[n3686]], and POLITICO.eu described France's parties as divided over cash for defence [[n3700]].
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Stay selective. Own the fiscal beneficiaries with visible order books, avoid chasing defence names after their 20-session run, and treat the euro's gain as a dollar call rather than a growth call. Autos stay in the middle until tariff clarity arrives. The stance turns Bullish if the Euro Stoxx 50 reclaims its 20-session reference of 5,390.91 once the defence exemption is adopted, which would show the fiscal story reaching the index. It turns Bearish if the German package stalls and the tariff drag returns to the headlines.

geo.label: stimulus hope / deflation drag
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. Stimulus is arriving in headlines faster than it arrives in prices. Bloomberg reported that China's inflation fell below zero for the first time in a year [[n1414]], and CNN's headline said deflation problems are getting worse [[n1458]]. CNBC said the $41 billion consumption plan 'is just a start' against deflationary pressures that are deepening [[n1449]]. The growth target was set at around 5%, alongside stimulus measures, as trade worries mounted [[n10535]]. Officials have said more stimulus is possible if growth slows [[n1247]], which tells you where the policy floor sits.
PMIs & Activity

The latest activity print in these headlines is February's non-manufacturing PMI, at 50.4 (China Daily, 1 March) [[n0915]]. That is a services reading just above the expansion line, which is not a boom. Retail is soft at the edges. A Reuters story described one store holding flash sales four times a day in deflation-hit China [[n1484]], and SCMP reported that Gucci and Prada are closing more China outlets as luxury spending shrinks [[n1423]]. The consumer-price series is the one to watch. January's CPI was up 0.5% (China Daily Global Edition, 9 February) [[n0632]], and the February reading that fell below zero is the more recent direction.
Credit Impulse

The latest credit print in the headlines is January's. Chinese bank lending hit a record high on policy stimulus [[n0748]], and that is the flow the stimulus narrative depends on. The bond market is pushing back. China's bond yields jumped to three-month highs as investors pared rate-cut expectations [[n1443]], and a strategist warned that more Chinese bond issuance to keep yields up will drain liquidity from markets [[n4039]]. For the impulse to hold, new lending has to keep pace with bond supply, and January's record is the bar. Some Hong Kong banks refusing home loans for Vanke's Le Mont project in Tai Po [[n1613]] show that property-linked lenders are still choosy about names.
Property

Property is the part of the story the official line talks up. A minister said the sector is showing positive changes [[n1413]], and Global Times relayed that the real estate market keeps stabilising on policy support [[n1416]]. The price data are less generous. Reuters reported that second-hand home prices narrowed their decline for a seventh straight month in February [[n0918]], which is still a decline, and WSJ's headline put it as a slight improvement that remains in decline [[n0780]]. The Financial Times argued the state is propping up the housing market [[n0869]]. Reuters also reported that China Evergrande and others were ordered to repay $1.8 billion of deposit pledges to a property unit [[n1568]], a reminder that the developer tail has not closed.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Policy is two stories. Beijing set its 2025 growth goal at around 5% and laid out stimulus as trade worries mounted [[n10535]], and economists told CNBC the goal will need much stronger stimulus if the US trade war intensifies [[n1241]]. On trade, Reuters reported that the US and China had discussed a Trump-Xi summit for June [[n1544]], and SCMP's insiders said Trump may meet Xi in China as soon as April [[n1467]]. That is a real de-escalation track. The other side is still active. Trump is targeting China-made containerships [[n1620]], and Bloomberg described China deploying food as a weapon in the trade war [[n1441]]. Chinese rapeseed meal and oil contracts surged after 100% tariffs on Canadian imports, per Reuters [[n1461]], which shows how fast the tariff map is moving.
Markets & Flows

Equities are pricing the policy story faster than the data. The Hang Seng closed at 23,782.14, up 11.68% over 20 sessions from 21,294.86, and the KWEB internet ETF is up 8.19% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,379.83, up 1.86% over 20 sessions, while USD/CNY sits at 7.2591, down 0.62% over the same period (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Flows are the crowd at the edges. Mainland investors snapped up a record amount of Hong Kong stocks to play AI [[n1488]], and Reuters reported that Chinese retail traders are embracing DeepSeek as a nod to quants [[n6605]]. The institutional side runs the other way: hedge funds cut China stocks for a fourth week as DeepSeek optimism faded [[n1475]].
New / Most Important

The most important item is the summit track rather than any data print. Reuters reported, citing the WSJ, that the two governments had discussed a Trump-Xi summit for June [[n1544]], and the WSJ's own exclusive said the same [[n1583]]. For Hong Kong and US-listed Chinese names, a confirmed summit is worth more than any PMI. The stimulus debate in the same headlines is about how much Beijing must add if the trade war intensifies [[n1241]], and a summit is the one thing that could shrink that need.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Treat the Hang Seng and KWEB exposure as a trade on the summit headline rather than a call on the economy, and size it for a reversal. Keep the yuan in your model at 7.2591 rather than assuming a stronger currency will carry the rally. Stay away from property developers and from banks whose books run through the property channel. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng's 11.68% gain over 20 sessions is running ahead of a deflation print that turned negative, so the equity rally is pricing a policy turn that the price data have not yet shown.

geo.label: hike bets / weak growth
parts: Macro Stance

Bearish for growth-sensitive Japan. The Nikkei 225 closed at 36,793.11, down 5.14% over 20 sessions from 38,787.02 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and SoftBank's shares are down 18.98% over the same window. The growth backdrop is softer than the rate story. Japan revised its fourth-quarter GDP lower, which complicates the BOJ's interest-rate outlook [[n3077]], and Reuters reported that US tariffs clouded the outlook as the downgrade landed [[n5432]]. The bond market is pricing the BOJ more than the economy: Japan's 10-year yield hit its highest since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [[n5429]].
Activity & Currency

Yen strength is doing tightening the BOJ has not yet done. USD/JPY closed at 147.0690, down 3.09% over 20 sessions from 151.7590 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and Nikkei Asia reported the yen hit a five-month high on expectations of a BOJ rate hike [[n5369]]. A strategist told Fortune that the yen is now the new safe-haven currency, arguing that nobody will trust a US treaty again [[n5397]]. Service-sector mood soured on the rising cost of living [[n5434]], and a tightening job market is pushing some firms under [[n3079]]. Tokyo Electron closed at 21,370 yen, down 16.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), so the export-equipment names feel the strong yen most.
Playbook ✓

Bearish. Keep Japanese exposure to domestic, rate-insensitive names rather than the export-equipment leaders, and use yen longs as the hedge against a risk-off leg. The BOJ is the event to track. Reuters reported that inflation risks may bring a rate hike into discussion in May, according to sources [[n5352]]. The call changes if USD/JPY closes back above its 20-session reference of 151.7590, which would mean the yen's strength has reversed and the export names get their relief.

geo.label: tariff exposure / weak tape
parts: Macro Stance

Bearish. The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,890.10, down 7.00% over 20 sessions from 8,484.00 and down 3.76% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The tariff exposure is what the market is pricing. The Guardian reported that Anthony Albanese denounced US tariffs as 'not a friendly act' after Trump refused an exemption for Australia [[n0432]], and ABC asked how a US recession could hit Australia [[n0451]]. BlackRock cut its exposure to Australian shares, citing their poor value [[n0359]], and the AFR argued the ASX sell-off is getting serious and blamed banks and passive investing [[n0331]].
Demand & Financing

Iron ore is the transmission channel, and it is under pressure. The AFR reported that China's cuts to steel production are piling pressure on Australian iron ore [[n0350]], although Reuters reported Singapore iron ore rising on optimism about Chinese demand [[n0467]]. The miners are trading that two-way price. The banks are the sharper read. Commonwealth Bank closed at 146.92 AUD, down 9.40% over 20 sessions from 162.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The Australian reported that the RBA's Michele Bullock is cautiously weighing a series of global storms [[n0328]], and the AFR reported that the RBA is alarmed about banks' plans to shut a key payments system [[n0463]]. AUD/USD closed at 0.6280, up 0.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), so the currency is not doing the adjusting.
Playbook ✓

Bearish. Underweight the banks into the tariff headlines, and hold the iron-ore leaders on a tight leash, because China's steel cuts are the driver the headlines keep returning to. Keep AUD as a funding currency rather than a risk currency. The call changes if the US grants Australia the exemption the headlines say is being refused. On the currency, AUD/USD would need to break its 20-session reference of 0.6271 to the downside to confirm a second leg lower.

geo.label: defence build-out, cautious rates
parts: Macro Stance

Bullish on the defence-led build-out, cautious on rates. Bloomberg reported in February that the zloty hit a 10-year high against the dollar, fanned by a hawkish central bank [[n5527]]. The real economy is improving in pockets. Notes From Poland reported that manufacturing shows signs of recovery for the first time in almost three years [[n5536]], and Eurostat put Poland's unemployment rate at a record low, joint-lowest in the EU [[n5546]]. Domestic data are mixed. Business Insider Polska reported a rise in unemployment and the labour ministry's explanation for it [[n6140]], and GUS data show Poles aged 35-44 earn the most [[n6152]]. Housing is turning: Strefa Inwestorów reported that apartment prices in Warsaw and Krakow fell year on year for the first time in three years [[n6163]].
Markets

The zloty is the swing factor. USD/PLN closed at 3.8703, down 4.61% over 20 sessions from 4.0572, but up 1.06% on the session, as Rzeczpospolita reported a sell-off in the zloty with the dollar and euro sharply higher [[n6138]] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). EUR/PLN closed at 4.1952, and wnp.pl's FX note said the zloty remained in a 4.10 to 4.20 band against the euro [[n6081]]. The dollar-denominated Polish ETF is the strongest read: EPOL closed at 26.88, up 9.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 49.08 PLN, up 1.89% over 20 sessions and 3.37% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Leadership is rotating. Orlen closed at 65.28 PLN, up 13.61% over 20 sessions, and Asseco Poland at 140.40 PLN, up 11.96%, while KGHM fell 5.70% and CD Projekt 6.51%. Dino Polska shares are at their highest in the company's history [[n5996]]. Bankier.pl reported that CCC and Zabka enter the WIG20 after the 21 March session, with Cyfrowy Polsat and JSW leaving [[n5931]], and Bloomberg reported that a billionaire is seeking approval for a share sale after CCC's stock tripled [[n5613]].
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is moving in Poland's favour, at least on the EU side. Rzeczpospolita asked whether Poland gains or loses as Brussels eases the excessive-deficit rules [[n5930]], and the paper's interview with Credit Agricole's chief economist, Jakub Borowski, quoted him saying the EU is moving toward loosening fiscal rules [[n6171]]. EU ministers backing a temporary defence-spending exemption is the same story seen from the member-state side [[n5614]]. Domestic politics is noisier. Bloomberg reported that a far-right candidate jumped to second in the Polish presidential race [[n5599]], and Bankier.pl quoted presidential candidate Biejat promising to bring order to the mortgage market [[n6075]]. The US has said it will retaliate if Poland introduces a tax on big tech [[n5610]], a revenue-side risk the headlines do not quantify.
Corporate & Sectors

Energy and defence are where the Polish story is concrete. Reuters reported that Ukraine's Naftogaz and Poland's Orlen will cooperate on LNG [[n5583]], Rzeczpospolita called the Orlen-Naftogaz deal important for Ukraine because it concerns a strategic commodity [[n6036]], and Money.pl reported that Orlen bought Starlinks for Ukraine and published what they cost [[n6182]]. The state is taking a bigger role in defence. GMK Center reported that Huta Czestochowa is becoming the property of the Ministry of National Defence [[n5618]], and Bankier.pl described a military battalion on the WSE, with exchange companies profiting from the military bull market [[n6013]]. Banks are the political target. Business Insider Polska wrote that big profits have become inconvenient and that banks are 'once again becoming punchbags' [[n5934]]. TotalMoney reported that deposit rates are falling while banks earn billions [[n6104]], and Bankier.pl reported that UOKiK is examining BIK scoring as a possible limit on banking competition [[n6122]]. KGHM's chief executive, in his first interview, described years of neglect and no investment [[n6041]].
Geopolitics & Security

Security is driving the fiscal story. Reuters reported that Poland wants 100,000 volunteers in military training in 2027 [[n5626]], and Euronews reported the plan to give every adult male military training [[n5586]]. Poland has asked NATO to raise its defence-spending minimum to 3% of GDP [[n5570]], and the New York Times quoted the premier saying that, alarmed by Trump, Poland must look at nuclear options [[n5557]]. AP reported that Poland and the Baltic states welcomed Macron's nuclear deterrent proposal [[n5551]]. The friction with Washington is real: Reuters reported Rubio telling Poland to 'say thank you' amid the Ukraine Starlink spat [[n5589]]. Bankier.pl put the reserve pool at more than 300 thousand people and asked how many the army could mobilise [[n5941]]. The Guardian reported that Ukraine agreed to a 30-day ceasefire as the US prepares to lift military aid restrictions [[n5053]].
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is the EU's defence exemption reaching Poland's budget arithmetic. EU ministers backed a temporary exemption for defence spending from the EU rules [[n5614]], and Rzeczpospolita's question on the easing of the excessive-deficit rules [[n5930]] is what turns that into room for Warsaw. If Brussels loosens the fiscal rules, the 3% of GDP defence minimum becomes a budget line rather than a campaign line. The second-order risk is the tax fight with Washington [[n5610]], which would be a revenue-side cost to set against the defence plan.
Playbook ✓

Bullish. Own the energy and defence-linked names that carry the trade, with Orlen as the cleanest expression of the Ukraine and LNG headlines, and keep zloty exposure hedged rather than long. Avoid chasing the WIG20 leaders into the index change after the 21 March session, when the flows will be mechanical. Watch the bank names for the regulatory tail. ⚠ Divergence: EPOL is up 9.45% over 20 sessions in dollars while the WIG20 total-return tracker is up only 1.89% in złoty, so the foreign-currency rally is doing the work and the local index is lagging.
Narrative

Technology is down on growth and valuation, not on a single earnings miss. The sector ETF closed at 208.40, down 11.78% over 20 sessions from 236.22 and down 4.62% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The AI capex story still carries the group's narrative, but the headlines are asking what it is worth now. Oracle is the bull case in one name: Reuters reported strong long-term growth as AI cloud demand soars [[n3196]], and Fortune counted $130 billion of contracts that exclude Stargate [[n3180]].
Reported

The results in the window were mixed. Oracle reported a sales rise and touted data-centre growth [[n3093]]. Marvell's shares tumbled despite strong AI revenue growth [[n3184]], after CNBC reported a near-20% plunge when its outlook fell short of high expectations [[n2879]]. Salesforce's slide this year is a headline of its own, down 15.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11) [[n3117]].
EPS Upside Watch

Oracle has the clearest revenue visibility in the headlines, with $130 billion of contracts already signed [[n3180]]. Marvell is the reset set-up: after a 23.97% drop over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), the bar is lower. ServiceNow's planned purchase of AI startup Moveworks for nearly $3 billion [[n3101]] lifts the growth narrative more than this year's EPS.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Oracle's outlook drew strong-growth headlines, and the stock still fell 3.10% in the 11 March session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The market is refusing to pay for AI growth it cannot yet see in margins. Meta's test of its own AI training chip [[n9140]] cuts against the consensus that the chip vendors are the only AI winners.
Narrative

Communication services are being sold on the platforms and the carriers at once. The sector ETF closed at 96.35, down 6.64% over 20 sessions from 103.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Meta is down 15.57% over 20 sessions and Alphabet 12.03%, so the advertising-led platforms are carrying most of the sector's weight into the sell-off. Alphabet's push to cut the cost of new nuclear with small reactor deployments [[n6498]] is a long-dated project that does not move the near-term revenue line.
Reported

The carriers flagged near-term softness in public. Telecom stocks fell after Verizon's comments at a Deutsche Bank conference [[n3210]], and AT&T and T-Mobile tumbled on the same day [[n3226]]. Stocktwits framed it as Verizon and AT&T sliding on signals of near-term softness, with retail divided [[n6657]]. Disney's shares sank as consumer sentiment sagged [[n9126]].
EPS Upside Watch

The carriers offer no clean upside set-up, because they are the ones signalling softness. The platforms are where a beat would matter. Meta's first in-house AI training chip [[n9140]] is a cost lever if it works. Filings showing Google's larger funding of Anthropic [[n9201]] are a disclosure, not an earnings line, so neither should be counted as EPS upside yet.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The platforms are the convention break. Meta is testing its own AI training silicon [[n9140]] while its shares sit 15.57% lower over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). That says buyers of the ad platforms are pricing a slowdown the chips cannot yet offset.
Narrative

Banks are trading the recession, not the balance sheets. The sector ETF closed at 47.61, down 7.39% over 20 sessions from 51.41 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Goldman Sachs is down 18.31% and Citigroup 16.39% over the same window. Yahoo Finance headlined the mechanism as bank stocks tumbling over rising recession fears [[n0532]], and fintech names fell on worries about consumer spending and credit [[n6520]].
Reported

The reporting that moved the group was regulatory and strategic, not earnings. Robinhood agreed to pay $29.75 million to end US regulator probes [[n6439]], and Morgan Stanley's Wilson warned that the S&P 500 could sink 5% on growth risks [[n4020]], a call on credit demand that lands on fee lines.
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is hard to argue this week. SoFi's Liz Young Thomas said the longer uncertainty goes on, the worse it is for guidance [[n6388]], and credit-sensitive names are where that bites first. Any bank that holds loan books through the tariff period is the set-up to watch, but the headlines do not yet show one.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Citi downgraded US stocks [[n11510]] while its own strategist kept a $6,500 base case for the S&P 500 at year-end [[n11568]]. The sell-side is mixing its signals. The bank that cut its rating still expects the index higher by year-end, which is the convention break in the group.
Narrative

Oil is the weak link and gas is the exception. WTI closed at 66.25, down 8.39% over 20 sessions from 72.32, and Brent at 69.56, down 8.32% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Gunvor's chief executive said at CERAWeek that global oil supply growth is outstripping demand [[n8508]], and that supply side is what the sector is trading. Henry Hub gas closed at 4.45 per MMBtu, up 29.30% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). At CERAWeek, natural gas was pitched as a tonic for power-hungry AI [[n9087]].
Reported

Energy reporting was about cost and strategy rather than beats. Exxon is betting on natural gas in its eighth Guyana oil project [[n9159]], and Pioneer Natural's chief executive spoke on tariffs, steel and oil prices [[n9377]]. Southwest Airlines is ending an oil hedge that once saved it billions [[n9437]], which is the cost side of the same oil story.
EPS Upside Watch

Oil-linked EPS faces a lower price deck, so the set-up favours gas-weighted names over crude. Microsoft said it is open to natural gas for its AI data centres [[n9314]], which is the demand line gas-weighted producers need. Crude-weighted names have to show volume growth to offset the price.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The sector is splitting along the gas-oil line, which cuts against the single 'energy as an inflation hedge' narrative. Crude fell 8.39% over 20 sessions while gas rose 29.30% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), so an investor who bought energy as inflation protection may have bought the wrong half of it.
Narrative

Industrials are split between the aerospace volume story and the tariff-and-travel drag. The sector ETF closed at 130.12, down 6.09% over 20 sessions from 138.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Aerospace is the exception. Boeing's shares rose 3.99% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), after Reuters reported that Boeing deliveries rose 63% in February from a year earlier [[n9079]].
Reported

Airlines cut their forecasts, citing consumer confidence and economic uncertainty [[n8938]], and the New York Times framed it as an early alarm about consumer spending [[n9001]]. Delta cut its profit forecast as uncertainty hit travel [[n3148]], and Southwest is ending free checked bags [[n9069]].
EPS Upside Watch

Boeing's volume is the upside lever. Deliveries up 63% year on year are a volume line that reaches the top line before it reaches margins [[n9079]]. The airlines are the reverse, with forecasts being cut, so the upside is one-sided by sub-sector rather than across the group.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Boeing's delivery rebound [[n9079]] runs against the airlines' guidance cuts [[n8938]]. Volume and demand are disagreeing inside one sector, and the group's stance stays Mixed until the two sides reconcile.
Narrative

Discretionary is being sold on the consumer. The sector ETF closed at 196.39, down 13.24% over 20 sessions from 226.35 and down 5.69% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Consumer confidence sank in the headlines [[n10843]], and Target's profit warning tied to Trump tariffs [[n3109]] has become the template for the group. Amazon is down 15.68% over 20 sessions, Home Depot 11.07% and Target 14.11% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Reported

Kohl's gave a rough outlook for the year ahead and its shares plunged 20% [[n3179]], with net sales falling nearly 10% in a quarter worse than Wall Street expected [[n0536]]. Target tanked on its first-quarter profit warning [[n3109]], and Abercrombie & Fitch was pummelled after predicting a tariff hit [[n6217]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is hard to argue for discretionary in these headlines. Best Buy's marketplace push is being read as an advertising story [[n3138]], which is the one lever in the set that could surprise. Several of the names in these headlines are being guided down.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla is the most-discussed discretionary name, and its shares are moving on the political backlash and the President's endorsement [[n9510]] rather than on consumer demand. That breaks the consumer-led narrative the rest of the group is trading.
Narrative

Staples are the one part of the consumer that has held up. The sector ETF closed at 81.47, up 2.04% over 20 sessions from 79.84 and down 0.77% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Procter & Gamble is up 3.34% over 20 sessions, Coca-Cola 10.05% and PepsiCo 5.53%, while Walmart is down 15.04% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The defensive bid is selective, and that selectivity is the story.
Reported

Staples reported mixed. Henkel's growth guidance disappointed as weak North America weighed [[n3690]], and Costco missed quarterly profit estimates on rising merchandise costs [[n2831]]. Dollar General's fourth-quarter report was previewed with earnings expected to decline [[n2838]].
EPS Upside Watch

Dollar General is the low-bar set-up. Its preview expected earnings to decline [[n2838]], and a later preview listed the factors to watch [[n0535]], so a result that merely holds would beat a lowered bar. Costco's set-up is the reverse, with its shares carrying lofty expectations [[n2951]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Costco's miss [[n2831]] came while the sector ETF rose over 20 sessions, so the rotation is not simply into premium quality. The group is rising while Costco's quarterly profit came in below estimates.
Narrative

Health care is two sectors. The sector ETF closed at 146.06, down 0.16% over 20 sessions from 146.30 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), but the spread inside it is wide. Merck is up 9.64%, AbbVie 12.21% and Johnson & Johnson 7.53% over 20 sessions, while Eli Lilly is down 5.16% and Novo Nordisk 6.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The weight-loss names are where the momentum is missing.
Reported

Illumina cut $100 million of costs and lowered its outlook because of a China sales ban [[n3065]]. Merck opened a North Carolina manufacturing facility amid Trump's tariff threats [[n4971]], and Hims & Hers is shutting its Apostrophe dermatology business [[n6619]].
EPS Upside Watch

Eli Lilly's launch of its weight-loss drug in emerging markets this year [[n4001]] is pipeline upside the stock is not paying for at present. That makes the 20-session laggard the most interesting set-up, provided the launch lands on time.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The weight-loss leader is lagging while the older franchises rally. Lilly is down 5.16% over 20 sessions and Novo 6.91%, against AbbVie up 12.21% and Merck up 9.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). That is a rotation out of the growth story inside a defensive sector.
Narrative

Materials are being pulled by tariffs in two directions. The sector ETF closed at 85.33, down 3.84% over 20 sessions from 88.74 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Copper closed at 4.74 per pound, up 4.69% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and Bloomberg reported that US factories are paying more for metal than overseas rivals because of tariff turmoil [[n9464]]. Iron ore is pulled the other way by China's steel cuts [[n0350]].
Reported

Trade policy is the reporting line. The Guardian reported that steel and aluminium tariffs came into effect amid the US-Canada trade war [[n5029]], and Reuters looked back at the last time Trump imposed the same tariffs [[n5065]]. Fortescue is down 17.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), the iron-ore name the steel cuts are hitting hardest.
EPS Upside Watch

Copper producers have the cleanest set-up in the headlines. BHP is putting $25m into the copper explorer Cobre [[n0421]], which is an investment signal rather than an earnings beat. Freeport rose 4.00% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), so the tariff premium is already in the price.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Copper is being bid as a tariff-proofed metal, an asset rather than a verdict on the economy, and that is the break from the iron-ore reading that China's steel cuts are dragging the group lower.
Narrative

Real estate is trading on housing deals, not on rates. The sector ETF closed at 41.62, down 0.98% over 20 sessions from 42.03 and down 3.25% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Rocket's $1.75 billion deal to buy Redfin [[n11033]] is the sector's loudest headline, and the argument is that it would consolidate home listings and mortgage lending in one shop [[n11036]]. Mortgage rates are down 37 basis points this year, according to Yahoo Finance [[n10961]].
Reported

The deal reporting is the only real company event in the group. Redfin's shares spiked on the announcement [[n11033]], and the consolidation case is about listings and lending rather than about rates [[n11036]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside is a call on housing turnover. Rocket's deal argues that listings and lending are worth more inside one company, which is an upside lever for the acquirer's margins rather than for the sector's aggregate earnings.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The one bid in housing is M&A. Redfin spiked on the deal [[n11033]] while the sector ETF was down 0.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), so the consolidation story is outperforming the sector's rate-sensitive core.
Narrative

Utilities are split by who owns the power. The sector ETF closed at 77.41, down 2.00% over 20 sessions from 78.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). PJM's transmission growth is rebounding, and datacentres are lifting the outlook for future expansion [[n11031]]. Texas is a data-centre job hotspot in the tech boom [[n11131]].
Reported

Utilities reported rate and cost questions rather than beats. Rocky Mountain Power is making the case for a rate hike, saying large users will pay more [[n9397]], and Utility Dive reported that insurance is unlikely to stop utility wildfire risks [[n3075]].
EPS Upside Watch

Dominion Energy is the set-up that Seeking Alpha frames around data-centre catalysts [[n3156]]. The regulated names are where upside is most traceable: rate cases raise the earnings base, and data-centre load is the reason the base is growing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Merchant power has broken from the regulated names. Vistra is down 32.09% and Constellation Energy 35.19% over 20 sessions, while Duke gained 1.82%, Southern 5.37% and NextEra 6.21% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The AI-power trade is being sold in the merchants and bought in the regulated utilities.
Narrative

European autos are a tariff story with a German fiscal bid. The sector ETF closed at 52.09 euro, up 1.86% over five sessions and down 0.13% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Volkswagen's US listing is up 21.47% over 20 sessions and BMW 10.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), while Stellantis is down 3.78%. Germany's car industry is bracing for Trump's tariffs [[n3568]].
Reported

Volkswagen expects revenue to grow in 2025 and says it feels 'all-American' as tariffs loom [[n3220]], but its profit is under pressure from tariffs and competition [[n3221]]. The Cariad software unit is set to lose 1,600 staff [[n4135]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen has the most visible restructuring set-up. The Cariad cuts [[n4135]] are a cost lever, and revenue guidance [[n3220]] gives the top line a floor. The upside is conditional on tariffs not rising, which is why the sector stays Mixed.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Volkswagen rose sharply over 20 sessions while the sector ETF was flat (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and it did so while profit pressure from tariffs was in the headlines [[n3221]]. The market is paying for German fiscal reflation rather than for the autos' own earnings.
Narrative

Semiconductors carry one of the sharpest drawdowns on the sector map. The sector ETF closed at 192.12, down 12.55% over 20 sessions from 219.70 and down 5.02% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The Philadelphia Semiconductor index closed at 4,374.07, down 13.94% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). TSMC is down 17.78% and Broadcom 19.12% over the same window, with Nvidia down 18.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Reported

Chip-supply headlines are a mix. Meta is testing its first in-house AI training chip [[n9140]], and Huawei reportedly acquired two million Ascend 910 AI chips from TSMC through shell companies [[n1482]]. ASML is building a reuse-and-repair centre in Beijing despite US-China tech tensions [[n5341]].
EPS Upside Watch

Memory has the longest runway in the headlines. Seeking Alpha frames Micron around a prolonged memory cycle [[n3185]], and Micron is down 7.17% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The set-up is a cycle argument at a lower price.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Business Insider reported that Nvidia's 30% sell-off has made it cheaper than when ChatGPT launched, at least by one metric [[n6543]]. That is a valuation argument against the sell-the-AI-trade consensus, and it is the signal the sector's price action has not yet adopted.

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance outranks the quarter
parts: Rewarded

Outlooks get paid when they are strong and the stock has room to move. Xeris Biopharma soared to a near four-year high on a strong 2025 outlook, and Stocktwits reported retail bulls charging in [[n6399]]. Ocugen's shares were lifted when its Q4 revenue crushed estimates, which Stocktwits framed as lifting retail confidence [[n6281]]. Hut 8 surged on a profit boom even though its Q4 revenue missed estimates [[n2556]].
Punished

Guidance cuts are where the punishment lands. Kohl's shares plunged 20% on a rough outlook [[n3179]], Target tanked on its first-quarter profit warning [[n3109]], and Delta's shares fell after it slashed its outlook on weaker US demand [[n3059]]. Marvell plunged nearly 20% when its outlook fell short of high expectations [[n2879]], and it tumbled again despite strong AI revenue growth [[n3184]]. Oracle is the test case of a strong outlook that still lost ground: Reuters reported a strong long-term growth outlook [[n3196]], and the stock still fell 3.10% in the 11 March session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Pattern

The market pays for the next quarter, not the last one. Strong numbers paired with a cautious outlook get sold, and a raised or merely stable outlook gets rewarded. Delta's cut and the wider airline forecasts share a cause the headlines name, economic uncertainty [[n3148]], which means the guidance language is carrying the reaction. Earnings reactions are now a read on tariffs first and on the quarter second.
Attention into EPS

The low bars are the ones to watch into the next prints. Dollar General's fourth-quarter preview said earnings were expected to decline [[n2838]], and a later preview listed the factors to watch [[n0535]]. Constellation Software's Q4 preview [[n0490]] uses the same pre-report framing. Summit Insights downgraded Nvidia amid AI market concerns [[n2506]], which sets the bar for the chip names' next guidance.
Playbook

Own the guidance, not the quarter. Favour names whose outlooks are being raised into a low bar, avoid names where a cautious outlook is the only news, and size the reaction risk around any print that lands during a tariff headline. The call changes if tariff headlines stop driving outlook language, which would show the reaction returning to the quarter itself.

underowned.title: Consumer staples: the defensive nobody is telling a story about
parts: Attention Gap

The tape is talking about AI and tariffs, not staples. The sector ETF is up 2.04% over 20 sessions while the S&P 500 is down 8.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and the headlines spend their energy on the chip and airline names. It is the one part of the consumer complex that is up over 20 sessions, and that is the gap.
Exposure & Risk

Name the instruments: the staples ETF and the large-cap names, Procter & Gamble (up 3.34% over 20 sessions) and Coca-Cola (up 10.05%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The risk is that the defensive bid is selective. Walmart is down 15.04% over the same window, so owning the group is not the same as owning the basket.
Trigger to Watch

The dated event is Dollar General's fourth-quarter report, previewed with earnings expected to decline [[n2838]]. A result that holds would be the signal that the group is being treated as a defensive again.

underowned.title: Regulated utilities, not the AI-power merchants
parts: Attention Gap

The AI-power story is told through merchant names with nuclear and gas optionality, and the headlines keep returning to gas for data centres, as with Microsoft's openness to it [[n9314]]. Regulated utilities get the same power demand without the headline. Duke, Southern and NextEra are up over 20 sessions while Vistra and Constellation are down more than 30% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Exposure & Risk

Name the instruments: Duke Energy (up 1.82% over 20 sessions), Southern Company (up 5.37%) and NextEra Energy (up 6.21%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The risk is regulatory. A rate case is only as good as the commission that approves it, and the Rocky Mountain Power request shows the trade-off between cost recovery and the bills large users pay [[n9397]].
Trigger to Watch

Data-centre load announcements that name a utility as the supplier are the observable event. The PJM transmission rebound and the datacentre outlook for future expansion are the first examples in the headlines [[n11031]].

underowned.title: The yen as the hedge the headlines call a safe haven
parts: Attention Gap

Fortune's strategist called the yen the new safe-haven currency [[n5397]], but the trade is discussed as a Japan story, not as a hedge for global equities. USD/JPY closed at 147.0690, down 3.09% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), which is the move the headlines have not yet turned into a theme.
Exposure & Risk

Name the instruments: USD/JPY spot and the yen currency ETF. Seeking Alpha argued that being short USD/JPY makes sense [[n4087]], which is the same trade from the other side. The risk is that yen strength is what hurts Japan's exporters first, and Tokyo Electron is down 16.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Trigger to Watch

The BOJ discussion of a rate hike in May is the event. Reuters reported that inflation risks may bring it into the discussion, according to sources [[n5352]], so the yen's direction into that meeting is the observable trigger.

underowned.title: Copper, bid as a tariff-proof asset
parts: Attention Gap

Copper's move is in the price, not in the commentary. Copper is up 4.69% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), while the headlines stay on the tariffs that are pushing US metal prices up [[n9464]]. Copper is being treated as an asset, and the attention sits on steel and aluminium instead.
Exposure & Risk

Name the instruments: copper futures and the copper miners ETF, COPX, which is down 5.87% over 20 sessions while the front-month copper price has held up (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The risk is the tariff path. The Guardian's headline on steel and aluminium tariffs coming into effect [[n5029]] shows how quickly the policy can move.
Trigger to Watch

Any tariff decision on the metals chain is the trigger, since the 50% Canadian steel and aluminium rate has already been pulled back once. CNBC reported it would not be imposed the next day [[n5031]].

crypto.title: Bitcoin is still the anchor, and altcoins are paying for the fall
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 82,862.21 on the 11 March UTC day, up 5.51% on the session and down 14.25% over 20 sessions from 96,635.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-11). Ether closed at 1,919.84, down 29.31% over 20 sessions. Solana closed at 125.26, down 25.88%, XRP at 2.17, down 20.94%, and Dogecoin at 0.16, down 35.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-11). The equity proxies fell further. Coinbase is down 31.59% over 20 sessions, Strategy 22.12% and the spot bitcoin ETF IBIT 14.70% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). CoinDesk recorded bitcoin at $76,700 as it filled another CME futures gap [[n1999]], and CNBC reported that it rebounded after falling to its lowest level since November [[n2006]].
New / Most Important

The most important item is plumbing, not price. Cantor Fitzgerald launched a $2 billion bitcoin financing business and picked Copper and Anchorage Digital as custodians [[n2012]], and Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream will offer bitcoin and ether custody [[n2027]]. The Clearstream custody launch is set for April [[n2019]]. Those are institutional rails being laid while the price falls. Coinbase's chief executive plans to hire 1,000 US workers, saying Trump 'breathed life back' into the industry [[n1925]].
Playbook

Bearish into the reserve headlines. Keep bitcoin exposure as a tradable bounce with a defined stop rather than a long-term add, until the 20-session reference of 96,635.61 is reclaimed. Avoid the bitcoin miners and the altcoins, which have fallen more than bitcoin: Ether is down 29.31% and Dogecoin 35.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-11). The equity leg follows the same logic, with Coinbase a bearish catalyst on the index snub.

flows.title: Liquidity is abundant and leaning into the front end
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is abundant on paper and selective in price. The New York Fed's Perli said market liquidity levels remain abundant [[n3769]], and the ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% [[n3489]]. The Fed is on hold in the headlines: Waller eyes interest-rate cuts this year but not this month [[n11253]], and Jamie Dimon called Trump's fixation with Jerome Powell somewhat to be expected [[n11552]]. The Bank of Japan is moving the other way. Talk of a rate hike in May [[n5352]] and a 10-year yield at its highest since 2008 [[n5429]] mean the liquidity pool is tightening at the margin. One strategist argued that more Chinese bond issuance will drain liquidity from markets [[n4039]].
Rates & Dollar

The curve is doing the work. Over 20 observations the 2-year is down 34 bps and the 10-year down 23 bps, with the spread 11 bps wider (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-11). The dollar index is down 4.51% over 20 sessions to 103.44 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11), and the Guardian reported euro and pound gains amid 'Trumpcession' fears [[n3679]]. In the bond ETFs, the 7-10-year sector (IEF, up 1.71% over 20 sessions to 94.71) and the 20-plus-year sector (TLT, up 1.57% to 90.40) have gained more than the 1-3-year sector (SHY, up 0.57% to 82.48) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The belly and the long end are bid. The 2-year's bigger yield fall is the policy repricing, and the ETF returns measure the same move differently.
Credit Check

Credit is where stress would show first, and the headlines are mixed. Bloomberg described a massive unwind that makes US junk bonds a riskier bet than Europe's [[n4104]]. HYG is down 0.80% over 20 sessions to 78.87, while investment-grade LQD is up 0.39% to 107.98 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The high-yield ETF has moved far less than equities over the same window, so the worry is about who is buying the risk rather than about the index price. Short-term bond ETFs are raking in billions amid recession alarm bells [[n4037]], and Insurance Journal reported that private credit's push for retail money stokes a new vulnerability [[n6630]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Fund flows are chasing safety and cutting risk. Hedge funds cut China stocks for a fourth week [[n1475]], and Reuters' sources said hedge funds fleeing positions dented European stock traders [[n3683]]. Bloomberg reported that Millennium's $900 million loss spells broader hedge fund pain [[n4055]]. Italian asset managers' net inflows doubled year on year to 6 billion euros in February [[n4101]], so some savers are still buying. The IPO window is open but wobbling. Venture Global's flop wiped out $38 billion of value after its listing [[n4052]], while Nasdaq's Adena Friedman says the IPO pipeline remains healthy [[n4022]].
Portfolio Implication

Own the front end and the belly, hedge equity beta, and keep the dollar underweight rather than long. The credit check says keep high-yield exposure small while HYG sits below its 20-session reference of 79.51 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The implication matches the US block: buy protection on the equity leg and let the curve carry the defensive trade. What changes it is HYG reclaiming 79.51 with the VIX back under 15.81, its 20-session reference, which would mean the stress is fading rather than rotating.

anticipatory.title: A Senate vote on the shutdown bill
parts: What Is Priced

The House has passed a bill to avert a shutdown and sent it to the Senate [[n11535]], and Senate Democrats face a choice that ABC called 'stark' [[n11499]]. The New York Times framed the House as daring the Senate to accept the bill [[n11534]]. The market is pricing a deal, with the risk concentrated in timing. The 2-year is down 34 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-11), which fits a market that treats a shutdown as a growth risk rather than a rates event.
Conditional Expression

If the Senate passes the House bill, the front-end bid loses urgency and the most beaten index names can bounce. Keep that as a tactical bounce rather than a rotation. If the Senate balks, hold the front end, keep the dollar underweight, and test the S&P 500 against its 5,572.07 close with protection bought before the vote.
Risk

The risk is a standoff that runs past the House vote while the labour data stay firm, which leaves the Fed with no reason to move. Job openings at 7.7 million [[n11142]] are the kind of print that keeps the cut debate on the back foot.

anticipatory.title: Canada, metals and a tariff threat that keeps coming back
parts: What Is Priced

Trump backed off a Canadian tariff hike after Ontario lifted its electricity threat [[n11587]], and CNBC reported that a 50% Canadian steel and aluminium tariff would not be imposed in the next session [[n5031]]. Reuters described the metals tariffs doubling and then backing off [[n5046]]. The market is pricing the threat as negotiable, which is why yields are falling rather than the dollar rising.
Conditional Expression

If the threat returns at the full 50% rate, metals producers and Canada-exposed industrials reprice, and the trade is to own US-made metal over importers. If the threat is withdrawn for good, the metals bid fades, and copper's tariff premium becomes the thing to watch.
Risk

The threat has no fixed end date, which makes the trigger hard to time. Bloomberg reported that Trump walked back the latest threat while playing down recession talk [[n5022]], so a reversal can come as fast as the threat did.

anticipatory.title: A June summit between Trump and Xi
parts: What Is Priced

Reuters reported that the US and China had discussed a Trump-Xi summit for June [[n1544]], and SCMP's insiders said Trump may meet Xi in China as soon as April [[n1467]]. Chinese equities have already moved, with the Hang Seng up 11.68% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). A good part of the optimism is in the price.
Conditional Expression

If a summit is confirmed, the trade is the Hong Kong internet names on their 20-session momentum, with USD/CNY steady near 7.2591. If the talks stall, the reversal is fast, because the rally is ahead of the price data.
Risk
China's inflation dipped below zero [[n1414]], and the stimulus must grow if the trade war intensifies [[n1241]]. The risk is a summit announced as a deal while the deflation data keep weakening.

anticipatory.title: Germany's spending package and the Ukraine ceasefire
parts: What Is Priced

Politico reported that Germany's Merz has two weeks to deliver a historic spending revolution [[n3562]], and EU ministers backed a temporary exemption on defence spending [[n5614]]. On Ukraine, the US and Ukraine called for a 30-day ceasefire after the Saudi talks [[n5038]], and the US said it would resume military aid and intelligence sharing [[n5041]]. Rheinmetall's 57.78% gain over 20 sessions shows how much of the package is already in the defence trade (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Conditional Expression

If the package passes on schedule and a ceasefire holds, the trade is to own the defence builders on the earnings path rather than on the headline. If the ceasefire fails, the defence premium is tested, and Central European risk assets, including Poland's, carry the Ukraine headline.
Risk
A ceasefire can lower the defence premium before the spending arrives. Russia said it was hit by a massive drone attack ahead of the talks [[n4988]], which shows how fast a headline can turn.

catalysts.title: $ORCL — the backlog is the thesis
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Oracle reported that its sales rose and touted data-centre growth [[n3093]], and Reuters reported a strong long-term growth outlook as AI cloud demand soared [[n3196]]. Fortune reported $130 billion of contracts that exclude Stargate [[n3180]]. The thesis is that the contract backlog turns AI demand into multi-year revenue visibility, which the market is not paying for while the sector trades on fear.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 144.18, down 3.10% on the session and 19.42% over 20 sessions from 178.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The hurdle is a reclaim of 178.92. The risk is that the sector's selling continues and Oracle falls with the tape.
Trade Expression
Long shares, in two tranches around the current close. Invalidated by a weekly close below 144.18 while the Nasdaq 100 is making lower lows.

catalysts.title: $BA — deliveries are the catalyst
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported that Boeing deliveries rose 63% in February from a year earlier [[n9079]]. The thesis is the volume recovery. Deliveries turn into cash, and the stock is priced for the opposite after airlines cut their forecasts [[n8938]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Boeing closed at 154.06, up 3.99% on the session and down 14.67% over 20 sessions from 180.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The hurdle is a reclaim of 180.55. The risk is that airline demand weakens faster than deliveries recover.
Trade Expression
Shares, or call spreads with a 6-month horizon. Invalidated by a close below 154.06 after the next airline forecast cut.

catalysts.title: $MRVL — the reset is the set-up
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reported that Marvell plunged nearly 20% when its outlook fell short of high expectations [[n2879]], and Yahoo Finance reported that its shares tumbled again despite strong AI revenue growth [[n3184]]. The catalyst is the expectations reset. The thesis is that the AI revenue line is intact while the multiple resets.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Marvell closed at 67.16, up 2.27% on the session but down 23.97% over five sessions and 40.46% over 20 from 112.80 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The hurdle is the 20-session reference of 112.80, which is far away. The risk is a second outlook cut.
Trade Expression
Wait. A stock down 40.46% over 20 sessions can fall further on one guidance line, so no new position until the next print shows the outlook has stabilised.

catalysts.title: $COIN — the snub is the catalyst
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Yahoo Finance reported that Coinbase fell 10% on crypto summit disappointment and an S&P 500 snub [[n11455]], while Expand Energy was picked to join the index [[n11407]]. The thesis is that index exclusion removes a bid, and the crypto summit delivered less than the market wanted.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Coinbase closed at 191.69, up 6.95% on the session but down 31.59% over 20 sessions from 280.22 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The risk is that the stock tracks bitcoin's bounce, and bitcoin rose 5.51% on the same session.
Trade Expression
Short shares, or buy puts against the bitcoin proxy. Invalidated by a close back above 191.69 with bitcoin above its 20-session reference of 96,635.61.

catalysts.title: $CRDO — the upgrade into the drawdown
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Stocktwits reported that Credo Technology gets an upgrade at Susquehanna as the stock halves from its peak, with retail 'extremely bullish' [[n6607]]. The thesis is that a rating change into a 43.75% drawdown over 20 sessions resets the entry point for AI connectivity exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).
Price Hurdle & Risk

Credo closed at 43.36, up 9.91% on the session but down 20.18% over five sessions and 43.75% over 20 from 77.08 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The hurdle is the 20-session reference of 77.08. The risk is that the chip sell-off continues, with the sector ETF down 12.55% over 20 sessions.
Trade Expression
Long shares, sized for a second leg down. Invalidated by a close below 43.36.

catalysts.title: $PLTR — insider sales meet a 33% drawdown
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Yahoo Finance reported how much stock Palantir's chief executive has sold [[n6353]], and Bloomberg reported that Palantir will expand AI across financial firms through the TWG venture [[n6284]]. The thesis is that insider selling into a drawdown signals the premium is being sold, while the venture news is the talking point the bulls will use.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Palantir closed at 78.05, up 2.19% on the session but down 7.52% over five sessions and 33.09% over 20 from 116.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The hurdle is the 20-session reference of 116.65. The risk is a squeeze on any AI-spending headline, which is what the session's bounce looked like.
Trade Expression
Bear call spread struck around the 116.65 reference. Invalidated by a close above 116.65.

retail_intro: The dominant popular-narrative trade is the Musk discount in Tesla, which has the shape of the GameStop squeeze, the Tesla run of 2020 and the 2020 to 2021 bitcoin rally: a famous name, a story the institutions doubted, and a crowd buying each drop as proof.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — the Musk discount is a buy
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's story is simple. Tesla is still the car, the battery and the charging network, so the drop is a political storm rather than a broken company. Business Insider put the feeling in one line: with the stock cut in half, Tesla investors want their CEO back [[n6587]]. The emotional hook is loyalty under siege. Trump called the boycott illegal and said he would buy a Tesla to support Elon Musk [[n9512]], which gave the crowd a cause to join. The number everyone anchors on is the half. Forbes headlined a 50% plunge and asked how to manage the volatility [[n6642]], which turns a drawdown into a discount. The hook follows: the stock fell because of the man, so it recovers when the man steps back.
What Is Driving It

The price is the first evidence. Tesla closed at 230.58 on the 11 March session, up 3.79% on the day, but down 15.24% over five sessions and 34.26% over 20 from 350.73 on 10 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Bloomberg reported that stocks rose before Trump met CEOs as Tesla jumped [[n11129]], and a day earlier CNBC reported Tesla shares plunging 15%, their steepest drop in five years [[n8803]]. Forbes put the move at a pre-election low and a $144 billion hit to Musk's net worth [[n11463]]. The backdrop is hostile but broad: the S&P 500 is down 3.57% over five sessions and the VIX is at 26.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). Tesla is the highest-beta expression of the political story. The demand counterpoint is China, where Yahoo Finance reported Tesla shipments tumbling, the latest sign of weakening demand [[n1521]].
The Social Signal

The social signal is loud and split. Business Insider reported that Tesla owners are offloading their cars over the Musk backlash [[n9470]], and another piece argued 'we're getting rid of our Tesla' and that the politics had nothing to do with it [[n8876]]. The crowd's counter-story is loyalty: investors want their CEO back [[n6587]]. Vandalism is the other signal. CNN reported acts of vandalism against Tesla facilities as anger against Musk mounts [[n8748]], and Fortune reported police barricading Tesla cars and dealerships as people rage against Musk's machines [[n11449]]. Musk's answer, that the protests are astroturfed by megadonors, shows the crowd is arguing about the cause as much as the stock [[n6518]]. The nearest retail-flow evidence is MarketWatch's warning that retail traders are getting spooked by the downturn, which is bad news for brokerage stocks [[n6553]]. The split is a loyal core buying the story and a wider circle exiting the car.
Historical Analog

The closest template is the GameStop episode, and Reuters used its label this month: a 'Gamestop effect', with retail traders behind Eutelsat's 650% surge [[n6322]]. The mechanics rhyme. A famous name is down, the institutions have written it off, and a crowd buys each leg down on the conviction that the story will be proven wrong. The second wave arrives after the first has already taken its gains, when mainstream coverage turns the trade into a cause. Here the amplifier is the presidency. Trump says he is buying a Tesla to support Musk [[n9510]], which is the mainstream moment the crowd has been waiting for. The analogy is about the mechanism, not the size of the move.
Smart Money View

The institutions are split on direction and on pace. Support comes from named bulls and long-term holders. Dan Ives, a Tesla mega bull, warned that Musk's patience is 'wearing thin' [[n6622]], which is a bull who is no longer comfortable rather than a bear. Ron Baron said he won't sell a single personal Tesla share amid the big decline [[n9398]]. Hedging and trimming come from the pension side. ABC reported that some pension fund managers worry as the stock falls [[n9056]], and New York State senators urged the comptroller to begin divesting pension funds from Tesla [[n9334]]. Baird's Ben Kallo said potential buyers may think twice if their cars are in jeopardy of being keyed [[n8484]], and Reuters asked whether Musk's EV party is over after years of the stock defying gravity [[n3112]]. The disagreement is less about direction than about pace. The bulls expect repair. The institutions expect a longer drawdown while the brand is contested.
When the Narrative Breaks

The breaks are observable. First, the levels: Tesla closed at 230.58 against a 20-session reference of 350.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). A bounce is only a bounce until the close climbs back toward that reference, and a close below the 11 March level would tell the crowd that the bounce was a headline rather than a bottom. Second, the demand data. Another weak China shipment print would make the political-storm thesis harder to hold, because it would mean demand is damaged, not just sentiment [[n1521]]. Third, governance. Musk has launched an appeal to restore a $56 billion pay package [[n9330]], and that appeal is a dated risk the headlines already show. Finally, the instrument risk is leverage. Leveraged single-stock products amplify every 5% move in both directions, which is how a 15% day turns into a forced seller's day.

retail.title: Quantum / IONQ — the next revolution after AI
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Quantum is the new 'next AI' a crowd can own with a ticker. Yahoo Finance asked whether quantum computing is the next revolution after AI [[n9386]], and a headline pitched a Magnificent Seven stock as joining the quantum revolution, with the hint that it is not Nvidia [[n6275]]. The conviction shows in the cashtags. IonQ halted its at-the-market programme after a $372M fund raise, and the stock rebounded pre-market while retail did not budge [[n6656]]. A leveraged ETF on IonQ's daily move was already listed for the crowd to trade [[n6614]].
Where It Breaks

IonQ closed at 18.70, up 2.35% on the session but down 16.33% over five sessions and 54.47% over 20 from 41.07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The break is supply. A raise of that size means the company sold into the rally, and every at-the-market programme is stock the crowd has to absorb. The science is the second break: New Scientist asked whether Microsoft is under fire for claiming a new quantum computer [[n8676]], and PCMag reported scientists questioning the same breakthrough [[n8773]]. Cramer's 'meme stock' label for Rigetti [[n6412]] shows the mainstream already sees the group as sentiment. Instrument risk: a 2x leveraged ETF compounds the daily move in both directions, so a bad week costs the leveraged holder far more than the unlevered one.

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC — the government reserve is the bid
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd treats the reserve as a standing buyer. Stocktwits reported that retail remains bullish after Trump announced a bitcoin strategic reserve instead of a diversified pool [[n1863]], and CNBC reported that bitcoin fell as much as 6.5% as volatility continued after the reserve plan [[n1882]]. The crowd reads that as a dip to buy, not a warning. The social side is the argument about the list. Yahoo Finance asked why the strategic crypto reserve did not include XRP [[n2091]], and the crowd can debate the list all day. The emotional hook is that the state is finally on the side of the coin.
Where It Breaks

Bitcoin closed at 82,862.21, up 5.51% on the session but down 14.25% over 20 sessions from 96,635.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-11). CoinDesk recorded a low of $76,700 as bitcoin filled another CME futures gap [[n1999]], which is the level the crowd will be watching. A close under that low would break the reserve story's floor. Coinbase's shares fell 10% on crypto summit disappointment [[n11455]], which shows the equity wrapper is more fragile than the coin. Instrument risk: the IBIT ETF is down 14.70% over 20 sessions, and the bitcoin miners are down more, with IREN down 45.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11).

retail.title: Rheinmetall / RHM — Europe is rearming, buy the tanks
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Rearmament is a story the crowd can understand in one sentence, and the tank builder is its ticker. Bloomberg reported that a tank builder's stock is now hotter than LVMH in the new European order [[n3693]], and the WSJ reported that overlooked European defence stocks became a hedge-fund home run [[n3640]]. In Poland, Bankier.pl reported that speculators moved their attention from Ukrainian stocks to steel and arms makers [[n6142]]. Rheinmetall closed at 1,154.00 euro, up 3.13% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The hook is the government as customer: the state is the buyer, so the earnings look guaranteed in the crowd's mind.
Where It Breaks

The trade has already priced much of the package. Rheinmetall is up 57.78% over 20 sessions from 731.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-11). The break is the package itself. Politico reported that Merz has two weeks to deliver the spending revolution [[n3562]], and EU ministers backing a temporary defence exemption [[n5614]] is the step that makes the money flow. A slip in either date, or a Ukraine ceasefire that lowers the threat premium [[n5053]], takes the air out. Instrument risk: a single-country defence name with a 57.78% move in 20 sessions is a crowded trade, and the stock trades in euros, so a US-based holder carries currency risk on top of the stock.
